Collaboration with Caltech aims at single‑protein mass spectroscopy and gravity‑mediated entanglement

jwst_massive_cosmic_structure.headline: James Webb Uncovers Ancient Galaxy Cluster XLSSC 122 Defying Cosmic Growth Models
jwst_massive_cosmic_structure.summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has detected the distant XLSSC 122 cluster, revealing an unexpectedly dense dark‑matter core that challenges standard cosmology.
highlights: XLSSC 122 lies 10.4 billion light‑years away and shows strong gravitational lensing
The cluster’s central mass concentration exceeds predictions for its early‑universe age
Intracluster light traces dark‑matter distribution, offering a new mapping tool

dna_recording_embryo_development.headline: DNA Typewriter Maps Mouse Embryo Development From First Two Cells to Organs
dna_recording_embryo_development.summary: Scientists used a DNA recording system to trace mouse embryogenesis for 13.5 days, revealing staggered cell‑type commitments and lineage imbalances.
highlights: DNA Typewriter recorded every cell division in a fertilized mouse egg for 13.5 days
The two founder cells produced similar mixes of cell types despite unequal descendant numbers
Blood and retina lineages committed early, while skin epidermis remained flexible longer

ocean_circulation_amoc_failure.headline: AMOC May Persist for Centuries Even After NADW Collapse, Study Finds
ocean_circulation_amoc_failure.summary: Using CESM2 and an idealized reduced‑gravity model, researchers show that cross‑hemispheric overturning can continue for centuries despite a complete shutdown of NADW formation.
highlights: CESM2 simulation with quadrupled CO₂ shows full NADW shutdown but only gradual slowdown of overturning
Reduced‑gravity model attributes sustained circulation to deepening of density layers
A clockwise overturning emerges in the Indo‑Pacific, altering heat and nutrient distribution
Ventilation age in the deep Atlantic is projected to increase substantially

early_universe_faint_glow_dark_energy.headline: CHIME Detects Faint Hydrogen Glow to Probe Dark Energy
early_universe_faint_glow_dark_energy.summary: Using CHIME’s new autonomous hydrogen mapping, scientists have measured a 2% neutral hydrogen signal from 5 billion years ago, opening a cheaper path to study dark energy.
highlights: CHIME captured the faint radio glow of hydrogen from 5 billion years after the Big Bang
The signal shows roughly 2% of hydrogen was neutral at that epoch
The instrument can now map hydrogen without relying on costly galaxy‑survey cross‑correlations

gluon_string_ion_sim.headline: Trapped Ions Simulate Gluon String Breaking, Challenging Classic Theory
gluon_string_ion_sim.summary: Researchers at Duke University used a trapped‑ion quantum computer to model gluon string breaking, confirming earlier results and suggesting tweaks to longstanding theory.
highlights: The experiment employed domain walls in a chain of trapped ions to represent quark‑antiquark pairs.
An external magnetic field triggered the creation of additional domain walls, mimicking particle production.
Results align with prior simulations on superconducting qubits (Google Sycamore) and neutral‑atom arrays (QuEra).
Findings indicate string breaking initiates at edges, contrary to the original Schwinger picture.

quantum_energy_ladder_observation.headline: Physicists Observe Predicted ‘Energy Ladder’ at Quantum Critical Points
quantum_energy_ladder_observation.summary: An international Caltech team used a laser‑trapped strontium atom quantum simulator to experimentally reveal the long‑theorized energy ladder at Ising and tricritical quantum tipping points.
highlights: Energy levels appeared as discrete “rungs” matching conformal field theory predictions.
Experiments employed up to 35 strontium atoms excited to Rydberg states.
Both the Ising and tricritical points showed universal spectra after size rescaling.
Measurements were published in Nature after 40 years of theoretical anticipation.

tiny_genome_microbe_discovery.headline: Tiny Archaea Sukunaarchaeum mirabile Sets Record with 238 kb Genome
tiny_genome_microbe_discovery.summary: A newly described microbe living inside Japanese plankton possesses a 238 kb genome, challenging definitions of life by approaching the minimal genetic requirements for independent replication.
highlights: Sukunaarchaeum mirabile was discovered inside the plankton Citharistes regius off Shimoda, Japan
Its genome of 238 kilobase pairs is the smallest known for any archaeon
The organism lacks most metabolic genes yet retains DNA‑replication and protein‑production machinery
Researchers propose it may be a parasitic archaeon, only the second of its kind recorded

dinosaurs_pole_shift.headline: True Polar Wander Shifted Earth’s Poles Up to 0.6° per Million Years During Dinosaur Era
dinosaurs_pole_shift.summary: New research shows Earth’s crust moved faster than thought, causing rapid pole shifts that altered climate and sea levels in the Jurassic and Cretaceous.
highlights: Four true‑polar‑wander events identified between 190‑20 million years ago
Sea‑level changes displayed a quadrupolar pattern across hemispheres
Shifts reached up to 0.6° per million years, faster than plate tectonics

juno_magnetodisk_rippling.headline: Juno Data Shows Jupiter’s Magnetodisk Ripples Like a Wave
juno_magnetodisk_rippling.summary: New analysis of Juno measurements reveals Jupiter’s magnetodisk repeatedly warps into wave‑like ripples during active reconnection events, challenging prior smooth‑disk models.
highlights: Juno crossed the current sheet multiple times per rotation, detecting repeated magnetic signatures and energetic particle bursts
The rippling structure spans roughly 100° of longitude and persists from several minutes to over an hour
These findings suggest the magnetodisk may influence the acceleration and transport of Io’s volcanic particles

planet_320_ly_away_chemical_similarity.headline: Ultra‑Hot Jupiter WASP‑189b Mirrors Host Star’s Magnesium‑Silicon Ratio
planet_320_ly_away_chemical_similarity.summary: Astronomers using Gemini South’s IGRINS spectrograph measured magnesium and silicon in WASP‑189b, finding a ratio identical to its star and confirming a key planet‑formation assumption.
highlights: First simultaneous detection of magnesium and silicon in an exoplanet atmosphere
Mg/Si ratio on WASP‑189b matches that of its host star
Observations made with high‑resolution IGRINS on Gemini South in Chile
Study published in Nature Communications (2026) and based on peer‑reviewed data

physicists_outran_quantum_tornadoes_to_p.headline: Physicists Outrun Quantum Vortices to Probe Superconductor Depairing Limit
physicists_outran_quantum_tornadoes_to_p.summary: Using 300‑femtosecond laser pulses, researchers at the Max Planck Institute pushed NbN and YBCO beyond their vortex‑driven limits to reveal intrinsic depairing thresholds.
highlights: Optical‑electric circuit generated picosecond current pulses that outran vortex dynamics by orders of magnitude
NbN (s‑wave) retained superconductivity until a sharp depairing threshold, while YBCO (d‑wave) showed gradual weakening
The method directly accessed gap symmetry, a property inaccessible to conventional DC transport

ai_reveals_chemical_shortcut_co2_fuel.headline: AI uncovers hidden 9,389‑reaction pathway boosting CO₂‑to‑methanol conversion
ai_reveals_chemical_shortcut_co2_fuel.summary: Researchers at Indian Institute of Science used AI to expand a copper catalyst network to 9,389 reactions, revealing a hydrogen pathway that raises CO₂ conversion by about 40‑fold.
highlights: AI‑driven model grew from 152 to 9,389 reactions on a copper catalyst
Expanded network correctly predicts methanol and CO as major products
Hydrogen can transfer as intact H₂, challenging traditional mechanistic views

turning_disorder_into_resource_wave_cont.headline: Disorder Engineered Acoustic Waveguide Achieves Non‑Abelian Braiding
turning_disorder_into_resource_wave_cont.summary: Researchers used the generalized Wigner‑Smith operator to arrange eighty metallic cylinders, enabling near‑perfect transmission and non‑Abelian braiding of acoustic modes.
highlights: Designed a scattering medium that performs target unitary transformations while preserving transmission
Demonstrated non‑Abelian braiding of waveguide modes in a compact acoustic waveguide only a few wavelengths thick
Showed that complex media can be programmed for diverse wave‑based information processing

ghostly_galaxies_dark_matter.headline: Ghostly Galaxies Lacking Dark Matter Challenge Modified‑Gravity Theories
ghostly_galaxies_dark_matter.summary: Three ultra‑diffuse galaxies—DF2, DF4 and DF9—appear to contain almost no dark matter, providing fresh evidence that dark matter is a real substance rather than a tweak to gravity.
highlights: DF2, DF4 and DF9 each show mass‑to‑light ratios consistent with ordinary matter alone
A June 2026 paper in The Astrophysical Journal proposes a head‑on collision that stripped dark matter from the progenitor galaxies
The findings undermine modified‑gravity models such as MOND and bolster the particle‑dark‑matter paradigm

moon_two_faces_solution.headline: Earth’s Gravity May Have Driven Moon’s Two‑Face Asymmetry, New Study Shows
moon_two_faces_solution.summary: Analysis of Chang'e‑6 far‑side rocks reveals uniform mantle composition but a magnesium‑rich crust, supporting a heat‑driven magma circulation model.
highlights: Chang'e‑6 returned far‑side anorthosite, Mg‑suite and basalt samples for the first time
Chemical signatures show mantle cumulates are similar on both hemispheres, while crustal rocks differ in Mg# and Th/Sm ratios
Researchers propose Earth’s tidal heating created horizontal magma flow, thickening the far‑side crust and concentrating KREEP
The peer‑reviewed paper appears in National Science Review (2026)

zombie_cells_protein_discovery.headline: Blocking PD‑L2 Halts Zombie Cell Build‑Up, Boosts Metabolism in Mice
zombie_cells_protein_discovery.summary: Researchers at Cedars‑Sinai found that inhibiting the protein PD‑L2 clears senescent cells, reducing inflammation and improving glucose handling and strength in aged mice.
highlights: PD‑L2 expression rises in senescent human cells and with age in tissues
Genetic deletion or antibody blockade of PD‑L2 cuts senescent cell accumulation in mice
Mice with reduced PD‑L2 show better blood‑sugar regulation and increased grip strength

hypernova_non_existence.headline: Study Shows Hypernova Explosions May Never Have Occurred
hypernova_non_existence.summary: New models suggest that irregular supernovae, not hypernovae, can explain the unusual chemical signatures of halo stars, challenging the need for ultra‑energetic explosions.
highlights: Researchers at University College London modeled asymmetric supernova ejecta and reproduced the odd element mixes of four
Analysis of a Milky Way halo red giant revealed heavy elements like silver and uranium without neutron‑star‑merger signatures.
The findings, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, argue that ordinary supernovae suffice to form

nepal_flood_seismic_analysis.headline: Seismic Study Pinpoints Timing of Nepal’s Deadly August Flood
nepal_flood_seismic_analysis.summary: Researchers used Nepal and Chinese seismometers to time the August 26 landslide at 8:37 a.m., revealing and possible precursor slide‑quakes.
highlights: The main mass movement began at 8:37 a.m. Nepal time, as determined from regional seismic data.
A magnitude‑2.5 event occurred 17 minutes before the collapse, but its role remains uncertain.
More than 60 small seismic events were recorded in the two weeks preceding the disaster, suggesting slide‑quake activity.
The collapse generated seismic amplitudes larger than the 2025 Tracy Arm landslide in Alaska.

2fle_catalog.headline: Second Catalog Reveals 450 Low‑Energy Gamma‑Ray Sources from Fermi‑LAT
2fle_catalog.summary: Using 14 years of Fermi‑LAT data, the 2FLE catalog lists 450 sources between 20 MeV and 200 MeV, highlighting dozens of new extragalactic and Galactic emitters.
highlights: 450 sources detected with TS>25 and median flux 1.9×10⁻¹¹ erg cm⁻² s⁻¹
377 sources associated with known counterparts, dominated by flat‑spectrum radio quasars (FSRQ)
60 newly discovered gamma‑ray sources, 51 at high latitudes, 38 exceeding 10σ significance
45 sources are TeV emitters and 6 coincide with 1LHAASO detections

act_dr6_alp_birefringence.headline: ACT Sets Tight New Limits on Axion‑Photon Coupling from Cosmic Birefringence
act_dr6_alp_birefringence.summary: Using five years of ACT polarization data, researchers find no time‑varying birefringence, tightening the axion‑photon coupling bound for ultra‑light dark‑matter candidates.
highlights: Analyzed over 10,000 time‑sliced polarization maps from 2017‑2022
Probed ALP masses from 2.5×10⁻²³ eV to 4.8×10⁻²⁰ eV
Set a 95% upper limit g_{φγ}<1.1×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹ (m_φ/10⁻²¹ eV)
Achieved the strongest stochastic‑field CMB bounds to date

arxiv_2610_19318v1.headline: JWST Maps Cosmic Star Formation from Today to Reionization Using Hydrogen Lines
arxiv_2610_19318v1.summary: A combined JWST/NIRCam slitless survey of COSMOS and GOODS‑N traces dust‑corrected hydrogen recombination lines in 9,146 galaxies, revealing star‑formation trends from $z\sim0$ to 9.
highlights: 9146 galaxies observed across $0.33\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ in COSMOS and $60.9\,\mathrm{arcmin}^2$ in GOODS‑N
Line‑flux limits reach $3.2\times10^{-18}$ and $1.04\times10^{-18}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}}$ for the two fields
Six hydrogen lines (Brα, Brβ, Paα, Paβ, Hα, Hβ) converted to equivalent Hα luminosities
Schechter fits show characteristic Hα luminosity rising toward cosmic noon

arxiv_2610_19926v1.headline: JWST Dormant Galaxies at z>3 Found Gas‑Poor, Likely Heading Toward Death
arxiv_2610_19926v1.summary: A study using ALMA archival data shows that JWST‑identified dormant galaxies at z>3 have molecular gas fractions far below main‑sequence expectations, indicating rapid quenching.
highlights: Dormant galaxies at z>3 display SFR10Myr lower than SFR100Myr, signaling a recent star‑formation drop
ALMA [CII]158µm and CO limits reveal gas fractions 0.3‑2 dex beneath main‑sequence levels
Gas fractions of dormant and quiescent samples are statistically indistinguishable
The sample spans COSMOS, UDS, and GOODS‑South fields with log(Mstar/Msun)>9.5

xray_superflares_protoplanetary_disks.headline: Chandra‑JWST Study Links Moderate X‑Ray Superflares to Disk Atmosphere Changes
xray_superflares_protoplanetary_disks.summary: Coordinated Chandra and JWST/NIRSpec observations of Orion Nebula stars reveal that moderate X‑ray superflares subtly alter infrared spectral features of protoplanetary disks.
highlights: Ten flare stars and twelve control stars were observed across six Chandra/ACIS-I and three JWST/NIRSpec epochs.
Variable narrow infrared features decrease with distance from the O star Theta1 Ori C, suggesting external irradiation effects.
HI Br‑alpha shows stronger variability and unique absorption‑core profiles in flare stars, indicating magnetospheric accretion
The CO fundamental band shows no flare‑related changes, matching thermochemical model predictions for moderate superflares.

2610_19881v1.headline: JWST MIRI‑MRS Reveals Distinct PAH Populations in Orion Bar
2610_19881v1.summary: Using blind signal separation, researchers extracted two mid‑infrared template spectra from JWST observations, distinguishing UV‑exposed and shielded PAH groups distinct.
highlights: Two template spectra named AIBirrad and AIBshield were derived via non‑negative matrix factorization
AIBirrad traces large, compact ionized PAHs strongly irradiated by UV radiation
AIBshield traces small, asymmetric neutral PAHs with aliphatic side groups in more protected regions
The study utilizes data from the PDRs4All program’s JWST MIRI‑MRS observations of the Orion Bar

2610_18975v1.headline: Modulated Phase Transition Could Seed Cosmic Curvature and GW Anisotropies
2610_18975v1.summary: A post‑inflationary first‑order phase transition, modulated by a light spectator field, may generate the observed large‑scale curvature perturbations and detectable GW anisotropies.
highlights: The mechanism reproduces the observed amplitude of curvature perturbations while predicting a loud stochastic GW background
Intrinsic GW anisotropies are strongly enhanced, falling within the sensitivity of space‑based detectors such as LISA, Taiji
The model yields a local primordial non‑Gaussianity signal potentially observable by upcoming large‑scale‑structure surveys

2610_18964v1.headline: Kerr Black Hole Spin Boosts EMRI Rates by Up to 2.5‑Fold
2610_18964v1.summary: New Monte Carlo simulations incorporating inclination diffusion show that Kerr spin can increase detectable EMRI events by roughly 2.5 times compared to non‑spinning models.
highlights: Inclination diffusion allows prograde orbits to become retrograde, altering EMRI‑to‑plunge outcomes.
Simulations predict a ~2.5‑fold rise in EMRI detections for rapidly spinning massive black holes.
Even without spin, relativistic Kerr geodesics raise EMRI counts by a similar factor.
The resulting inclination distribution shows a strong prograde bias, aiding future EMRI identification.

ilmt_transient_discovery_2026.headline: Indian ILMT discovers supernova candidates, DOT provides spectroscopic confirmation
ilmt_transient_discovery_2026.summary: The 4‑m International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT) identified several photometric transients, which were classified as supernovae through follow‑up spectroscopy with the 3.6‑m Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT).
highlights: ILMT continuously surveys a 22.3′ × 22.3′ zenith strip, enabling nightly transient detection
PyLMT pipeline uses optimized image subtraction and CNN classification to flag candidates
DOT spectra confirmed the supernova nature of the selected transients
Combined ILMT light curves with ZTF data improve photometric characterization

2610_19009v1.headline: Euclid Finds First L‑type Substellar Object Near Embedded Cluster NGC 2023
2610_19009v1.summary: A young L3 dwarf, J054158.70‑021031.4, was spectroscopically confirmed by Euclid near NGC 2023, with a mass at the planetary‑mass boundary.
highlights: Spectral type L3 with Av = 3 mag reddening
Optical magnitude ≈ 24.5 in Euclid band
Distance estimated at 403 pc, placing it near the planetary‑mass limit
Proper motion aligns with nearby cluster NGC 2024

brain_implants_voice.headline: Brain Implants Restore Voice for ALS Patient Casey Harrell
brain_implants_voice.summary: A brain‑computer interface implanted in Casey Harrell’s speech motor cortex has enabled him to speak again after ALS robbed his natural voice.
highlights: Implanted four electrode grids on the left precentral gyrus in 2023
Harrell has generated nearly 2 million words using the system, reported in Nature Medicine
The decoder initially used a 50‑word vocabulary, later expanded to over 125,000 words

magnetic_fossils_deep_ocean_oxygen.headline: Magnetofossils Reveal Absolute Deep‑Ocean Oxygen Levels Past
magnetic_fossils_deep_ocean_oxygen.summary: Researchers linked nanoscopic magnetic fossils to present‑day oxygen concentrations, creating an equation to estimate absolute oxygen levels in ancient deep‑sea environments.
highlights: Analyzed over 200 modern ocean sediment samples from global basins
Documented shapes of more than 4,500 magnetite grains using a transmission electron microscope
Found that low‑oxygen waters host more bullet‑shaped magnetite, while high‑oxygen waters favor tiny cubic crystals

engineered_multi_resistance_fungal_defen.headline: Engineered Plant Immune Receptors Offer New Defense Against Blast Fungus
engineered_multi_resistance_fungal_defen.summary: Scientists engineered tandem kinase receptors to recognize multiple blast fungus effectors, paving way for durable resistance in rice, wheat and barley.
highlights: Modified TKP immune receptors now bind two distinct effectors from Magnaporthe oryzae
Structural analysis revealed HMA domains act as bait for fungal attack molecules
Dual‑specificity receptors could be stacked with NLRs for layered crop immunity

2610_18998v1.headline: JWST Reveals Convective‑Transition Gap in Globular Cluster 47 Tucanae
2610_18998v1.summary: Deep JWST imaging of 47 Tucanae uncovers a narrow convective‑transition gap along the lower main sequence, confirmed by stellar luminosity function analysis.
highlights: The gap appears as a sharp dip followed by a sudden rise in star counts in two independent colour‑magnitude diagrams.
Empirical likelihood modelling shows the feature is statistically significant beyond random fluctuations.
Additional JWST passbands reproduce the discontinuity, strengthening evidence for a genuine stellar structure.

brain_activity_under_anesthesia.headline: Anesthetized Brain Still Analyzes Language and Predicts Words, Study Finds
brain_activity_under_anesthesia.summary: Even under full general anesthesia, patients' hippocampi processed word categories and forecast upcoming words, revealing sophisticated unconscious neural activity.
highlights: Neuropixels probes recorded activity from hundreds of hippocampal neurons during anesthesia.
Neurons distinguished unexpected tones and showed plasticity despite lack of conscious awareness.
Distinct patterns encoded nouns, verbs, adjectives and predicted next words in spoken stories.
Findings published in Nature (2026) challenge assumptions about consciousness and may inform brain‑computer interfaces.

chemical_starter_kit_life.headline: ALMA Finds Deuterium‑Rich Methanol and Masers in Young Star Disks
chemical_starter_kit_life.summary: Using ALMA, the COMPASS survey detected deuterium‑enriched methanol and widespread maser emission in the planet‑forming disks of eleven low‑mass protostars.
highlights: Methanol (CH3OH) was found with deuterium in the disk of IRAS 4A2, a protostar in the Perseus Molecular Cloud.
Methanol maser emission was detected around more than half of the surveyed protostars, the first such observation in low‑mass
The study surveyed eleven nearby low‑mass protostars, revealing variations in oxygen‑ and nitrogen‑bearing molecules across the
Results were published in seven papers in the October 2026 issue of Astronomy & Astrophysics.

melting_permafrost_arctic_rivers.headline: Melting Permafrost Drives Acid Rock Drainage in Arctic Rivers
melting_permafrost_arctic_rivers.summary: Long‑term monitoring shows sulphate and zinc spikes in Brooks Range streams after the unusually warm 2019 winter, linked to oxidative weathering of thawed permafrost sulfides.
highlights: Sulphate concentrations rose sharply in rivers draining the Brooks Range
Zinc levels increased concurrently, indicating mobilization of sulfide minerals
The 2019 winter warmth triggered rapid permafrost thaw and exposure of acid‑producing rocks
Similar chemical shifts have been reported in Yukon watersheds, suggesting a broader regional impact

2610_20948v1.headline: JWST Links ULX Ho II X‑1 to Highly Ionized Nebula in Holmberg II
2610_20948v1.summary: JWST IFU spectroscopy resolves a 15‑25 pc nebula around ULX Ho II X‑1, detecting [Ne V] and [Ne VI] and revealing anisotropic ionization linked to radio jets.
highlights: First detection of [Ne V] and [Ne VI] emission from the ULX nebula.
Highest‑ionization lines originate from compact regions offset toward known radio knots.
Emission lines are narrow, indicating quiescent gas and ruling out shock‑driven ionization.
Ionization extends over ~100 pc, showing the ULX’s black hole powers extreme nebular excitation.

desi_dr1_lrg2_model_independent.headline: DESI DR1 LRG2 Analysis Yields Model‑Independent Distance and Growth Measurements
desi_dr1_lrg2_model_independent.summary: Using a new emulator that varies power‑spectrum shape, DESI DR1 LRG2 data provide Alcock‑Paczynski and growth rate constraints consistent with flat ΛCDM.
highlights: Gaussian‑process emulator trained on N‑body simulation templates enables simultaneous fitting of shape, distance and growth
Measured Alcock‑Paczynski parameters α⊥ and α∥ and growth rate fσ8 differ by less than one‑twentieth of their uncertainties when
Projected onto flat ΛCDM the results give Hubble constant h = 0.724 ± 0.017 with χ² = 0.7 for two degrees of freedom

arxiv_2610_21628v1.headline: Richness Shapes Thermal Sunyaev‑Zel'dovich Signals in Galaxy Halos
arxiv_2610_21628v1.summary: A study of 7 million DESI Legacy Survey galaxies finds that thermal Sunyaev‑Zel'dovich pressure profiles vary with richness, challenging universal feedback models.
highlights: Thermal Sunyaev‑Zel'dovich Effect detected down to halo masses of 10^{12.2} M_⊙ at 5.8σ using ACT and Planck data
Mass‑richness bins show both standard GNFW profiles and flatter, mis‑centered profiles with β ranging from 1.3 to 5.49
In low‑mass, low‑richness halos the thermal energy‑mass relation deviates from self‑similarity by 7.3σ, making them key

hi_rotation_curves_568_galaxies.headline: Apertif Survey Delivers Largest HI Rotation Curve Sample of 568 Galaxies
hi_rotation_curves_568_galaxies.summary: The Apertif Wide-area Extragalactic Survey released 568 reliable HI kinematic models, providing rotation curves that span 20–300 km/s and extend up to 60 kpc.
highlights: 568 galaxies yield rotation curves with 3–23 data points each, peaking at four points.
HI disks cover three orders of magnitude in HI mass and reach radii of 2–60 kpc.
The HI mass‑size relation for 213 galaxies shows a slope of 1.96 ± 0.03 with scatter ~0.101 dex.
Intrinsic scatter of the relation is only 0.067 ± 0.007 dex, indicating nearly constant average HI surface density.

nonlocal_gravity_desi_constraints.headline: DESI Data Tighten Limits on Nonlocal Gravity Model Near ΛCDM
nonlocal_gravity_desi_constraints.summary: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation measurements constrain the Maggiore‑Mancarella nonlocal R □⁻² R gravity model, showing it aligns closely with the ΛCDM paradigm.
highlights: The nonlocal parameter maps to a specific (w₀,wₐ) trajectory in the CPL plane.
Implemented the model in a Boltzmann solver and ran MCMC with CMB, supernova, and DESI BAO data.
DESI BAO results push the nonlocal parameter toward the ΛCDM limit.
No statistically significant evidence favors deviations from standard cosmology.

2610_20714v1.headline: Pristine Survey DR2 Delivers Metallicities for 15 Million Stars to G≈20.5
2610_20714v1.summary: The second data release of the Pristine survey provides photometric metallicities for 15 million FGK stars down to magnitude G≈20.5, expanding coverage to 8,000 deg².
highlights: Covers ~8,000 deg², adding 1,500 deg² since DR1.
Includes >200,000 very metal‑poor and >6,500 extremely metal‑poor star candidates.
Calibrated with Gaia DR3 synthetic CaHK photometry via the PhotCalib neural network.
Validated against DESI metallicities, showing good agreement.
Reaches faint limit G≈20.5, three magnitudes deeper than previous release.

dust_cosmic_dawn_2026_10_16.headline: ALMA2040 to Reveal Hidden Dust and Star Formation Beyond Redshift 8
dust_cosmic_dawn_2026_10_16.summary: A next‑generation sub‑millimeter array, ALMA2040, will boost sensitivity tenfold, enabling routine detection of dust emission in galaxies at z > 8 and quantifying obscured star formation.
highlights: ALMA2040 offers an order‑of‑magnitude sensitivity increase over current ALMA
Will measure dust masses, temperatures, and infrared luminosities of early galaxies
Simultaneous far‑infrared line observations will probe supernova versus grain‑growth dust production
Enables assessment of how much star formation JWST‑identified galaxies miss due to dust

2610_20730v1.headline: ALMA2040 to Reveal Birth of Star‑Forming Clumps in Early Galaxies
2610_20730v1.summary: The upcoming ALMA2040 array will resolve individual giant molecular clouds in galaxies beyond redshift 1, linking cold gas to star‑forming clumps observed by JWST and HST.
highlights: ALMA2040 will achieve sub‑mm sensitivity and angular resolution sufficient to detect GMCs at cosmological distances
CO and [CII] line imaging will map molecular gas mass, temperature, and dynamics in lensed and unlensed galaxies
Combined with JWST and ELT observations, the program will connect dust, gas, and young stars across Cosmic Noon to the Epoch of
The study will test whether clumps arise from disk instability or external disturbances, informing models of galaxy evolution

deep_sleep_muscle_fat_brain.headline: Deep Sleep Triggers Hormone Circuit That Builds Muscle and Sharpens Brain
deep_sleep_muscle_fat_brain.summary: A newly mapped hypothalamic circuit shows deep non‑REM sleep drives growth hormone release, which in turn regulates wakefulness and metabolism, researchers report.
highlights: Neurons in the hypothalamus coordinate GHRH and somatostatin activity during non‑REM and REM sleep
Growth hormone feeds back to activate locus coeruleus neurons, influencing the transition to wakefulness
The circuit was identified using implanted electrodes and optogenetic stimulation in mice
Findings were published in Cell and may guide therapies for metabolic and neurological disorders

jwst_wasp17b_atmosphere_bulge.institution: NASA / James Webb Space Telescope Team
jwst_wasp17b_atmosphere_bulge.headline: James Webb Maps Lopsided Atmosphere on Hot Jupiter WASP-17b
jwst_wasp17b_atmosphere_bulge.summary: Using JWST, astronomers discovered that the atmosphere of WASP-17b bulges on its evening side, revealing extreme winds reshape hot‑Jupiter atmospheres.
highlights: The bulge appears on the planet’s evening limb, where winds transport heat from the day‑side to the night‑side.
The discovery was made with a new ‘transmission strings’ technique that maps atmospheric thickness at different angles.
Observations were part of JWST’s TST DREAMS Guaranteed Time program and are published in Nature Astronomy.
WASP‑17b lies 1,300 light‑years away and is a classic hot Jupiter orbiting very close to its star.

exoplanet_weather_jwst.headline: Webb Telescope Uncovers Ordered Weather Patterns on Distant Brown Dwarf
exoplanet_weather_jwst.summary: Using JWST data, researchers found that the turbulent brown dwarf SIMP 0136 exhibits three recurring atmospheric states driven by temperature shifts and cloud structure.
highlights: Principal Component Analysis identified two dominant components—temperature fluctuations and vertical cloud changes—explaining
Three distinct weather states rotate into view, alternating between hotter thin‑cloud regions and cooler thick‑cloud layers.
The method offers a rapid first‑step tool for analyzing JWST observations of brown dwarfs and giant exoplanets.

brain_cells_cognitive_decline.headline: Dysfunctional Oligodendrocytes Linked to Age‑Related Cognitive Decline
brain_cells_cognitive_decline.summary: Scientists found that aging oligodendrocytes produce abnormal myelin, damaging nerve fibers and accelerating memory and thinking decline in older adults.
highlights: Abnormal myelin buildup and loss of large nerve fibers were observed in brains of participants with faster cognitive decline
Reduced NRF2 protein in oligodendrocytes caused excess myelin and impaired learning in mouse models
Drugs that activate the NRF2 pathway are already used for multiple sclerosis, suggesting a repurposing opportunity

necklace_atoms.headline: Physicists Freeze Atomic 'Necklaces' to Reveal Century‑Old Bethe Strings
necklace_atoms.summary: Using ultracold cesium atoms in one‑dimensional tubes, researchers observed Bethe string clusters, confirming a quantum prediction made by Hans Bethe nearly a century ago.
highlights: The team cooled tens of thousands of cesium atoms into a Bose‑Einstein condensate and confined them in thousands of 1D tubes.
By tuning a magnetic field they switched inter‑atomic interactions from repulsive to attractive, enabling formation of strings
Measured expansion energies showed the one‑dimensional clouds retained about one‑third of the energy of three‑dimensional

nightjar_wing_tradeoff.headline: European Nightjar Trades Speed for Agility, Generates Upstroke Thrust
nightjar_wing_tradeoff.summary: Scientists at Lund University found that the European nightjar sacrifices high‑speed efficiency for agile hunting and uniquely produces thrust during the upstroke.
highlights: Wind‑tunnel tests showed broad wing tips improve slow‑flight maneuverability but reduce lift efficiency at higher speeds.
The nightjar’s upstroke actively generates forward thrust, a mechanism previously documented mainly in bats and insects.
These trade‑offs in wing design could inform the development of more efficient flapping‑wing drones.

new_research_reveals_how_long_stays_in_s.headline: Microgravity Shows Subtle Genome Changes After One Day, Study Finds
new_research_reveals_how_long_stays_in_s.summary: A NYU team using a Random Positioning Machine discovered that 24‑hour simulated microgravity modestly enlarges cell nuclei but leaves DNA organization largely intact.
highlights: Microgravity increased nuclear volume without altering nuclear envelope thickness
Fluid flow, not microgravity, caused observable DNA damage
Advanced imaging and 3D algorithms minimized confounding fluid effects

roman_telescope_performance.headline: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope delivers image quality 30% better than expected
roman_telescope_performance.summary: Engineers’ minute mirror tweak boosted the Wide Field Instrument’s performance, achieving 63 nm RMS optical error, nearly 30% above predictions.
highlights: Secondary mirror moved by one‑sixteenth of a human hair
Wide Field Instrument now reaches 63 nm RMS, surpassing the 90 nm target
Optical performance improvement translates to sharper cosmic surveys

alcohol_immune_brain_damage.headline: Alcohol Triggers Microglia to Destroy Brain’s Extracellular Matrix, Study Finds
alcohol_immune_brain_damage.summary: A mouse study shows that alcohol activates microglia to dismantle the brain’s extracellular matrix, leading to synaptic loss and heightened sedation.
highlights: Microglia reshape and shrink within one hour of ethanol exposure in mice
Activated microglia engulf and digest extracellular matrix components, weakening structural support
Silencing the immune protein MyD88 reduces matrix damage and sedation in genetically engineered mice
Human brain tissue from six alcohol‑use‑disorder cases shows similar matrix disruption

climate_records_congo.headline: Handwritten Archives Reveal Century‑Long Warming Trend in Congo Basin
climate_records_congo.summary: Digitized 9,000 handwritten logs from 37 stations show the DRC’s average temperature rose 0.5 °C since 1961, with extreme heat days nearly doubling by the 1980s.
highlights: The Yangambi archive contains over 9,000 pages of daily meteorological records dating from 1908 to 2023.
During 1961‑1990 average temperatures rose 0.5 °C and maximums increased about 0.7 °C.
Hot‑extreme days were almost twice as frequent in the 1980s compared to the 1960s.

redwoods_heat_photosynthesis.headline: Heat Stresses California Redwoods, Slowing Photosynthesis and Carbon Storage
redwoods_heat_photosynthesis.summary: New JGR Biogeosciences study shows that extreme heat raises redwood leaf temperatures, directly reducing photosynthetic rates and threatening long‑term carbon sequestration.
highlights: Leaf temperatures rose up to 18 °F above air on hot days in Garcia River Forest.
Fluorescence measurements revealed a decline in photosynthetic efficiency even when stomata remained open.
Field data from 2022‑2024 indicate redwoods cannot thermoregulate effectively under >100 °F conditions.
The peer‑reviewed paper predicts reduced carbon storage as regional temperatures continue rising.

third_form_magnetism_prize.headline: Third Form of Magnetism Wins 2026 Europhysics Prize
third_form_magnetism_prize.summary: Physicists have identified altermagnetism, a hidden third magnetic order, earning the 2026 Europhysics Prize and promising advances in spintronic technologies.
highlights: Altermagnetism adds a new symmetry class to ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism
Theoretical framework was built between 2016‑2024 at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz
Experimental confirmation came via ARPES and transport measurements in multiple crystals
The discovery was honored at CMD32 in Graz, Austria

fractional_fermi_sea.headline: Physicists Engineer Exotic Fractional Fermi Sea in Ultracold Cesium Atoms
fractional_fermi_sea.summary: A team led by Hanns‑Christoph Nägerl and Alvise Bastianello created a highly excited yet ordered quantum state, the fractional Fermi sea, using ultracold cesium atoms.
highlights: Repeatedly cycling interaction strength between strong repulsion and attraction drives one‑dimensional cesium atoms into the
The state exhibits hidden order manifested by Friedel oscillations and anomalous correlation decay, defying Tomonaga‑Luttinger
Theoretical results published in Physical Review Letters lay groundwork for an experimental realization currently under peer

sex_differences_skin_repair.headline: Sex Hormones Drive Distinct Skin Stem Cell Behaviors in Male and Female Mice
sex_differences_skin_repair.summary: Researchers tracked skin stem cells in live mice for five months, revealing coordinated renewal in females versus independent activity in males, linked to sex hormones.
highlights: Female skin stem cells synchronize division and differentiation, accelerating early wound closure
Male testosterone promotes faster stem cell maturation but reduces proliferation and coordination
Castrated males and ovariectomized females adopt the opposite sex’s cellular patterns when hormone levels are altered
The phenomenon was observed using advanced live‑imaging microscopy and confirmed in human skin organoids

dbs_depression_pathways.headline: Three White‑Matter Pathways Predict Lasting Relief in Depression DBS
dbs_depression_pathways.summary: A study of the largest SCC DBS cohort shows that stimulation of the cingulum bundle, forceps minor, and medial uncinate fasciculus predicts sustained improvement in treatment‑resistant depression.
highlights: Stimulation of the cingulum bundle, forceps minor, and medial uncinate fasciculus/ventral amygdalofugal pathways correlated with
Patients who failed to improve after two years lacked adequate activation of the left cingulum bundle.
Connectome‑based targeting guided electrode placement in the ongoing Abbott TRANSCEND randomized trial.
The analysis combined electrical‑field modeling with generalized brain connectivity maps across multiple international cohorts.

mmx_launch_earthsky.headline: JAXA’s MMX Mission Launches to Sample Mars Moon Phobos
mmx_launch_earthsky.summary: Japan’s MMX spacecraft lifts off on Oct 19, aiming to land a rover on Phobos, collect soil, and return the sample to Earth by 2031.
highlights: Launch from Tanegashima Space Center at 19:41 UTC on Oct 19, 2026.
Mission includes propulsion, exploration, and return modules, with a rover to drill Phobos soil.
Sample return capsule will land in Australia for retrieval in 2031.
MMX follows JAXA’s Hayabusa2 asteroid‑sample mission, extending Japan’s sample‑return expertise.

primordial_power_spectrum_from_the_lense.headline: New Iterative Delensing Method Sharpens Primordial Power Spectrum from CMB Temperature Data
primordial_power_spectrum_from_the_lense.summary: A novel NIRL‑FLIP algorithm iteratively removes lensing effects and applies Fourier denoising, enabling model‑independent reconstruction of the primordial power spectrum from CMB temperature measurements.
highlights: NIRL estimator updates lensing contribution using the free‑form PPS from the previous iteration.
FLIP low‑pass filter suppresses noise overfitting in Fourier space.
Simulations show bias reduction and noise suppression by a significant factor.
Method provides robust uncertainty estimates via bootstrap realizations.

hidden_disruption_mw_satellites.headline: Extended Stellar Mass Ratio Reveals Hidden Tidal Disruption in Milky Way Satellites
hidden_disruption_mw_satellites.summary: Using the Auriga simulations, researchers show that the extended mass ratio μ_EMR uncovers widespread tidal disruption among Milky Way satellite galaxies previously thought intact.
highlights: Traditional shape and proper‑motion indicators fail to reliably flag disruption in simulated satellites.
The ratio of stellar mass between 3 r₁/₂–10 r₁/₂ to that within r₁/₂ strongly correlates with tidal stripping.
Applying μ_EMR to observed Milky Way satellites suggests many are currently undergoing significant disruption.
Extended stellar distributions provide a new, mass‑independent tool for detecting hidden tidal effects.

arxiv_2610_23806v1.headline: JWST Little Red Dots Favor Standard Halo Formation Over Primordial Black Holes
arxiv_2610_23806v1.summary: Analysis of JWST LRD abundance and clustering from redshift 4 to 8 shows the conventional dark‑matter halo model matches observations, while primordial black hole seeds do not.
highlights: Observed clustering of JWST LRDs at z=4–8 aligns with predictions of virialized dark‑matter halos
PBH scenario requires a negligible mass fraction and predicts clustering far below the measured signal
Any subdominant early‑forming seed must be tied to massive host halos to reproduce the observed clustering

2610_23395v1.headline: Neutron-Star-Merger r‑Process Abundances Sensitive to Nuclear Level Density Uncertainties
2610_23395v1.summary: A new study shows that variations in nuclear level density models, more than gamma‑ray strength functions, significantly alter predicted r‑process element abundances from neutron‑star‑merger ejecta.
highlights: Final abundances depend more on nuclear level density (NLD) prescriptions than on gamma‑ray strength function (GSF) models.
Specific NLD choices create a sub‑peak at A=172‑178 and systematic shifts at A=180‑194 in the ejecta composition.
Sensitivity peaks in the cold r‑process regime and at intermediate electron fractions, where neutron captures dominate after

dust_in_galaxies_at_z_10_15_attenuation_.headline: FirstLight Simulations Reveal Dust Growth Patterns in z=10‑15 Galaxies
dust_in_galaxies_at_z_10_15_attenuation_.summary: Radiative‑transfer modeling of 99 early galaxies shows dust‑to‑metal ratios rise sharply near 0.2 Z⊙, favoring small silicate grains and hotter infrared emission.
highlights: Metallicity‑dependent DTM models reproduce ALMA dust‑mass upper limits at z≳10 and detections at lower redshifts
SMC‑like dust grains best match the observed UV‑slope β_UV≈‑2.3
Dust peak temperatures reach 60‑80 K, higher than the 40‑50 K assumed in many ALMA estimates
Detectable ALMA fluxes (10‑20 µJy) require UV‑bright galaxies with M_UV≲‑21.5

a_unified_solution_to_the_low_mass_x_ray.headline: Saturated Magnetic Braking and Irradiation Winds Solve LMXB Diversity Puzzle
a_unified_solution_to_the_low_mass_x_ray.summary: A new SMB+IDW model links magnetic saturation with irradiation-driven winds, reproducing LMXB accretion rates, ultracompact formation, and MSP orbital periods without fine‑tuning.
highlights: The SMB+IDW framework couples magnetic saturation directly to donor‑star winds driven by X‑ray irradiation.
It matches the full observed range of accretion rates for both persistent and transient low‑mass X‑ray binaries.
It naturally generates ultracompact X‑ray binaries, addressing a long‑standing formation gap.
It accurately reproduces the orbital period distribution of descendant millisecond pulsar binaries.

gravity_limited_acceleration_smbh.headline: Gravity-Limited Fields Around Supermassive Black Holes Could Accelerate Particles to 10^27 eV
gravity_limited_acceleration_smbh.summary: A new model shows that horizon‑scale magnetic fields limited only by gravity can propel cosmic rays to ultra‑high energies without extreme black‑hole spins or super‑Eddington accretion.
highlights: Universal ceiling on electromagnetic energy density near rotating SMBHs yields particle energies up to ~10^{27} eV
Curvature losses cause primary energy to scale weakly as E_curv ∝ M^{1/4} across SMBH masses 10^6–10^{10} M_⊙
Cross‑correlation with Pierre Auger Observatory data shows marginal local excesses (<2.8σ) for quiescent galaxies hosting

dark_matter_halos_horndeski.headline: Vainshtein Screening Weakens Inside Core‑Like Dark Matter Halos, Study Finds
dark_matter_halos_horndeski.summary: Researchers analytically and via N‑body simulations show that Vainshtein screening is less effective near halo centers, causing discrepancies among mass proxies.
highlights: Analytic conditions reveal screening breaks down as halo profiles become core‑like.
N‑body simulation of an isolated halo demonstrates biased hydrostatic, Jeans, and lensing mass estimates.
Discrepancies indicate a fifth force beyond Newtonian gravity on halo scales.
Study uses Horndeski theory with Vainshtein mechanism to probe modified gravity.

stat_gilead_s_ibd_drug_eliminated_sympto.headline: Gilead’s oral emvistegrast clears ulcerative colitis symptoms in Phase 2 trial
stat_gilead_s_ibd_drug_eliminated_sympto.summary: In a Phase 2 study, a daily 200 mg dose of emvistegrast achieved a 23% placebo‑adjusted remission rate in patients with moderate‑to‑severe ulcerative colitis after 12 weeks.
highlights: 200 mg emvistegrast taken daily for 12 weeks
23% placebo‑adjusted clinical remission in ulcerative colitis
Phase 2 trial met statistical significance
Gilead senior VP Swati Tole called results encouraging

topological_defects_cosmic_shear.headline: Topological Defects Boost Cosmic Shear Constraints in Euclid Simulations
topological_defects_cosmic_shear.summary: A new method using topological defects in the cosmic shear orientation field yields up to 3.9‑times tighter Ωₘ and σ₈ constraints than traditional weak‑lensing analyses.
highlights: Defect statistics derived from shear phase complement amplitude‑based weak lensing measures
Number density and clustering of defects characterized across simulated sky maps
Fisher analysis shows combined defect and convergence data dramatically improve parameter precision
Euclid‑like survey simulations demonstrate up to 3.9‑fold tighter Ωₘ and σ₈ bounds

scientists_win_2026_nobel_prize_for_cont.headline: 2026 Nobel Prize Honors Optogenetics Breakthrough Controlling Brain Cells with Light
scientists_win_2026_nobel_prize_for_cont.summary: A Nobel-winning discovery using channelrhodopsin lets researchers switch neurons on and off with light, enabling memory activation and potential therapies for vision loss and brain disorders.
highlights: Channelrhodopsin from the alga Chlamydomonas was engineered into mouse neurons to create light‑gated ion channels.
Optogenetics allows precise, millisecond‑scale activation of specific brain circuits via thin optical fibers.
Early clinical trials are testing optogenetic therapy to restore vision in patients with retinal degeneration.
The technique is being explored as a treatment avenue for Parkinson’s disease and epilepsy.

ai_quasi_riemann_hypothesis.headline: OpenAI AI Proves Quasi‑Riemann Hypothesis, Shaking Number Theory
ai_quasi_riemann_hypothesis.summary: OpenAI’s AI system delivered a proof of the quasi‑Riemann hypothesis, narrowing zero bounds to 1/12–11/12 and sparking intense mathematical scrutiny among researchers.
highlights: The proof shows all non‑trivial ζ‑zeros lie in the strip 1/12 ≤ Re(s) ≤ 11/12.
It was announced among 377 OpenAI papers on October 6, 2026, and the 49‑page version is the only one edited by a human.
Leading number theorists such as Jared Duker Lichtman, Maksym Radziwiłł, Peter Sarnak, and Alexander Dunn are rapidly verifying

new_3d_form_of_carbon_made_in_the_lab.headline: Swedish Team Synthesizes Diamondiyne, a New 3D Carbon Allotrope
new_3d_form_of_carbon_made_in_the_lab.summary: Researchers at University of Gothenburg created diamondiyne, a porous 3D carbon crystal formed at low pressure using a controlled cascade reaction on a liquid‑liquid interface.
highlights: Diamondiyne is the first carbon allotrope besides diamond with covalent bonds in all three dimensions.
Synthesis employed a cascade reaction at a liquid‑liquid interface between tetra(triethylsilylethynyl)methane and CuF2.
Resulting films cover ~5 cm² and range from several to tens of nanometres thick, confirmed by TEM over 10 nm³ volumes.
The work is reported in peer‑reviewed Angewandte Chemie and builds on prior graphdiyne and COF research.

apoe4_alzheimer_mechanism.headline: APOE4 Gene Variant Triggers Fat Buildup, Boosting Alzheimer Risk
apoe4_alzheimer_mechanism.summary: A new Cell Stem Cell study shows that APOE4 impairs Wnt signaling, causing lipid droplets in oligodendrocytes and increasing late‑onset Alzheimer’s disease risk.
highlights: APOE4 raises Alzheimer risk three‑ to twelve‑fold by disrupting fat transport in brain cells
CRISPR screen identified the Wnt pathway and DKK1 as key regulators of lipid accumulation in APOE4 oligodendrocytes
Blocking a downstream enzyme restored Wnt signaling, reduced cholesterol droplets, and improved myelin production in mouse models

biosignatures_top_km.headline: Biosignatures Detected Throughout Top Kilometer of Sedimentary Basins
biosignatures_top_km.summary: A new analysis shows δ13C signatures in CO₂, methane, and oil gravity persist down to one‑kilometer depth where microbial cells thrive.
highlights: δ13C of carbon dioxide and methane remains measurable to one‑kilometer depth
Oil gravity anomalies correlate with high microbial biomass
Low‑permeability layers suppress water infiltration and biosignature expression

equatorial_pacific_warming_adjustment.headline: Two‑Phase Pacific Warming Reveals Initial Gradient Strengthening Then Weakening
equatorial_pacific_warming_adjustment.summary: Model simulations under an abrupt 4×CO₂ scenario show the equatorial Pacific SST gradient first intensifying before gradually weakening due to slow ocean adjustments.
highlights: Initial SST gradient strengthening driven by equatorial ocean circulation changes and remote Northern‑Hemisphere atmospheric
Long‑term gradient weakening linked to slow oceanic adjustments after the fast response phase
Findings derived from AGU Advances peer‑reviewed study by Olonscheck and Kang using abrupt 4×CO₂ simulations
